title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 19
paragraphs: Themistocles, however, had conceived the idea that if the Ionian and Carian contingents could be detached from the barbarian force, the Greeks might overcome the rest. When the Euboeans were driving their flocks down to the shore, he assembled the generals and told them he thought he had a scheme by which he hoped to draw away the best of the king's allies. This matter he revealed only that far; as for their present circumstances, he said they should do the following: each man should slaughter as many of the Euboean flocks as he wanted, since it was better that their army should have them than the enemy; moreover, he advised that each commander should have his own men kindle a fire, and that he himself would see to the timing of their departure in such a way that they would come safely home to Greece. They were content with this, and at once, having kindled fires, they turned their attention to the flocks.
